skill.name: convex-suggest
skill.description: Spot custom implementations that a Convex component or built-in feature could replace. Suggest one option after the current task and install it only with explicit consent.
skill.summary: Get one Convex recommendation tied to your code or request.
skill.author: convex

remediation.suggestion: Verify the package and installation steps against official Convex documentation. Show the exact steps and obtain separate approval for changes outside the approved component.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format a slash command in Markdown, not a Ruby or shell expression. The workflow requires explicit consent before installation.
The inline counter expression illustrates how to cite the user's code. It is not a command or an instruction to evaluate the expression.
Email and SMTP are cues for recommending Resend. The rule does not send mail or instruct the assistant to connect to an email service.
The reference to fs.write is a cue for recommending Convex Storage. It is not a filesystem call or an instruction to write files.

content.value_statement: Custom backend code can duplicate features that Convex already offers. This skill suggests one relevant option after your task and explains what it could replace.
actual_capabilities: Matches patterns in Convex code snippets or user requests to documented recommendation rules.
Recognizes examples such as shared counter updates, scheduled jobs, database rate limits, and long-running actions.
Recommends built-in Convex Storage or full-text search when the observed code fits.
Suggests one option after the current task, cites the trigger, and provides an installation hint when applicable.
Skips options that are already installed and does not repeat a declined or ignored suggestion.
limitations: Does not offer recommendations for generic coding questions unrelated to Convex.
Relies on visible code or stated intent and does not perform a comprehensive dependency audit.
Does not benchmark performance or verify that a recommendation fits every project constraint.
Requires explicit consent before installing a recommended component.

use_cases.title: Review a shared counter
use_cases.description: Find out whether a sharded counter fits a Convex mutation that updates the same document under concurrent traffic.

use_cases.title: Assess a custom upload flow
use_cases.description: Check whether Convex Storage fits an application that currently sends attachments to an external storage service.

use_cases.title: Plan a background job
use_cases.description: Evaluate one relevant Convex component for a job with multiple steps or a concurrency limit.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Convex snippet
prompt_templates.scenario: Review one piece of custom backend logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Convex mutation. After the review, recommend one component if it matches the shared counter update. Do not install anything.

prompt_templates.title: Review a scheduled job
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess a recurring process during a bug fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix the scheduling bug in this Convex task. Afterward, tell me whether the Convex crons component fits this recurring job.

prompt_templates.title: Assess search requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Decide whether built-in search meets a project need.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my hosted search integration and its requirements. Explain whether built-in Convex full-text search fits. Note any requirements you cannot verify.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a backend recommendation
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose one option in a project with several custom patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the import job and installed Convex components. After the review, recommend one missing option. Use job duration, retry requirements, and concurrency limits to explain your choice. Wait for explicit approval before installation.

output_examples.input: Our Convex mutation updates the same post's like count every time a user clicks Like.
output_examples.output: Consider @convex-dev/sharded-counter. Your likes mutation updates one shared count, so concurrent requests can conflict. A sharded counter spreads those writes across multiple documents. No component was installed.

output_examples.input: Our Convex app uses a hosted search service only to match words in article titles.
output_examples.output: Consider built-in Convex full-text search. Matching words in article titles is the only search requirement you described. A Convex search index could cover that requirement without a separate service.

best_practices: Provide the relevant Convex snippet or describe the behavior you want.
List installed components and state any requirements the replacement must meet.
Verify the proposed package and installation steps against official documentation before approval.
anti_patterns: Interrupting the current task to suggest a component.
Repeating a recommendation after the user declines or ignores it.
Treating interest in a recommendation as approval to install it.

faq.question: When does the skill offer a recommendation?
faq.answer: It offers a recommendation after the current task when it sees a matching pattern in Convex code or in your request.

faq.question: Will the skill install a component automatically?
faq.answer: No. It waits for explicit approval before starting installation.

faq.question: Can it suggest built-in Convex features?
faq.answer: Yes. The rules include Convex Storage for file uploads and built-in full-text search for matching text.

faq.question: Can it recommend more than one component?
faq.answer: It offers one recommendation at a time unless you ask for more.

faq.question: Will it recommend an installed component?
faq.answer: No. It skips components it knows are already installed. Share your component list if it is not visible.

faq.question: Does it verify that a component meets my requirements?
faq.answer: No. The suggestion is based on the code or request it sees. Check the documentation and test the component before replacing existing logic.
